History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
31-year-old postpartum woman with sudden onset dyspnea one hour ago, four weeks after C-section, tachycardia on self-pulse count, advised to attend hospital urgently to rule out thromboembolism.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Acute shortness of breath while resting and watching TV.  
• Onset/Durations: Began ~1 hour prior to call; first episode.  
• Course/Progression: Not clearly worsening during call; patient feels anxious with “heart really going.”  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Dry cough started yesterday, no sputum.  
  – Palpitations (awareness of rapid heartbeat).  
  – Mild chest soreness on deep inspiration; C-section incision also tender.  
• No frank chest pain, no hemoptysis mentioned.  
• No previous similar episodes.  
• Review of systems otherwise unremarkable in transcript.

Past Medical History:
• Cesarean section 4 weeks ago; recovering, incision tender.  
• No other chronic medical conditions reported.

Medications:
• Codeine – dose/route/frequency not documented; last taken ~1 week ago.  
Allergies:
• Ibuprofen – reaction type not recalled.

Social History:
• Lives with partner (currently at work); caring for newborn at home.  
• No tobacco, alcohol, or recreational drug history mentioned.

Family History:
• Mother with history of leg blood clots (DVT).

Physical Examination:
• Heart rate: Patient counted 30 beats during clinician-timed interval (exact duration not documented); clinician interpreted as “slightly fast.”  
• No other vitals or physical findings available.

Investigations:
• None performed during virtual visit.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Acute dyspnea, postpartum (4 weeks) with tachycardia – concern for pulmonary embolism / thromboembolism.  
  Plan:  
  • Advise immediate evaluation in Emergency Department.  
  • Discussed option of ambulance vs self-transport; patient chose self-transport with infant.  
  • Instructed to go “fairly quickly” and bring baby supplies.  
  • Explained risk of clots after C-section and potential need for treatment (anticoagulation).  

Issue 2: Post-operative pain management.  
  Plan:  
  • Hold further codeine until evaluated.  
  • No NSAIDs due to ibuprofen allergy.  

General Plan items:  
• Patient given opportunity for questions; none.  
• Safety-net advice provided; patient agreed to attend hospital.  

Quality checks:

• Missing expected elements: full vitals, complete ROS, medication doses, obstetric history details, immunizations, detailed allergy reaction.  
• Internal conflict: Date of birth stated as “20 Apr 1980”; clinician repeated “1983” – conflict noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio with minor conversational filler; no inaudible sections.
